chunked-output-and-log-writers: The TS runner streamed each stdout and stderr chunk to the caller's logWriters and onOutput as it arrived, and wrote a 'Wine Command: ...' header when the child started (the logWriter and output events of the goldens). The Rust run_wine_command returns the captured output once the child ends, capped at MAX_BUFFER per stream, and writes no game log: the caller that owns a log writer (Phase 88, the launch path) writes the header and the returned text. The result, spawns and tree are the golden's.
command-parts-not-mutated: The TS runWineCommand mutated the caller's commandParts array in place, unshifting the proton verb and the wrapper list into it (87-08 finding 3, commandPartsAfter in the goldens). The Rust function takes its arguments by value and builds the argv on its own copy, so a caller's list is never changed. The argv each case spawns is the golden's.
track-and-resolve-on: The TS runner registered each wine child under track { runner: 'wine', key } for killTracked and resolved on 'close' or, with resolveOnExit, on 'exit' (the track and resolveOn fields of the runOptions events). The Rust spawn seam has no tracked registry: the child is a Helper registered with GameLib's child set, ended by a cancel token, the shutdown token or the exit path. trackKey and resolveOnExit are accepted and ignored until Phase 88 owns launching a game, which is what needs killTracked. The spawn trace, replaceEnv and timeouts are the golden's.
